term.ajuda:
openTARS {versao} · local AI assistant for Linux

Chat
  opentars                        open the chat in the terminal (continues the last one)
  opentars --new                  start a new conversation
  opentars --resume               pick a saved conversation to continue
  opentars --plan                 plan mode: the AI only describes what it would do
  opentars --auto                 edits in this folder without asking (delete, send and install still ask)
  opentars --chat "request"       answer one request and exit
  opentars -p "request"           for scripts: only the answer (or --output-format json); reads stdin
  opentars-gui                    open the window
  opentars-gui --rapido           open the quick bar (ctrl+alt+space)

Models
  opentars --model <name>         use this model with -p
  opentars --explicar "request"   show how the task and the model are chosen
  opentars --avaliar-classificador  measure how often Murph and automatic mode are right

Environment
  opentars --diagnostico          check Ollama, screen and accessibility (changes nothing)
  opentars --autoteste            diagnosis + a real test with the calculator
  opentars --setup                install whatever is missing (Ollama, models...)

Preferences
  opentars --idioma <code>        change the language (pt_BR or en)
  opentars --atalho [keys|off]    show, change or remove the global shortcut
  opentars --version              show the version

Inside the chat, /help lists the commands. An AGENTS.md in the folder goes into every conversation.

chat.dica: /help for commands · ctrl+c stops an answer · /exit leaves
chat.ajuda:
Commands
  /models               lists the installed AIs
  /model <name>         pins an AI (e.g. /model gargantua, /model the smallest)
  /model auto           back to automatic choice
  /resume               picks a saved conversation to continue
  /compact              summarizes the start of the conversation (frees context)
  /context              shows how much context is in use
  /mode <mode>          ask, plan (only describes) or auto
  /undo                 reverts the file edits of the last request
  /init                 creates an AGENTS.md with the project instructions
  !<command>            runs a shell command (its output goes to the next request)
  /clear                starts a new conversation
  /language <code>      changes the language (pt_BR or en)
  /unload               unloads every AI from memory
  /help                 shows this list
  /exit                 quits

Shortcuts
  ctrl+c                stops the answer (twice in a row: quits)
  ↑ ↓                   previous requests
  ctrl+r                searches previous requests

pu.modo.titulo: How much do you want to see?
pu.modo.texto: Choose the window mode. You can change it later in Settings > General.
pu.garg.lite_nota: This computer has no graphics card with 4 GB and little memory: we download Gargantua Lite (0.6 GB, with vision), which is lighter and makes a few more mistakes. It looks at the screen to find buttons, with less precision than Gargantua 2 (1.6 GB).
perigo.pergunta_sessao: Run it anyway? (y/N, or "always" for this command in this session)
codigo.pergunta: Apply it? (y/N, or "always" for edits in this folder this session)
codigo.pergunta_fora: This file is outside the project folder. Apply it? (y/N)
cli.contexto: ~{usados} of {total} context tokens ({modelo}). The count is approximate.
cli.contexto_cheio: The context is filling up: /compact summarizes the start of the conversation.
cli.shell_demorou: The command took over 2 minutes and was stopped.
cli.compactando: Summarizing the start of the conversation…
cli.compactada: Done: ~{antes} → ~{depois} tokens. The last requests were kept whole.
cli.nada_a_compactar: The conversation is still short: nothing to summarize.
cli.modo.perguntar: Ask mode: openTARS asks before changing files and before risky commands.
cli.modo.plano: Plan mode: the AI only describes what it would do. Nothing that changes anything runs.
cli.modo.automatico: Auto mode: file edits inside this folder do not ask. Deleting, sending and installing still ask.
cli.nada_a_desfazer: No edits to undo in this session.
cli.agents_criado: Created {arquivo}. Edit it freely: it is included in every conversation in this folder.
cli.agents_existe: There is already an AGENTS.md here; I left it alone.
cli.print_vazio: No request: use opentars -p "request" or send the text through stdin.
probes.sub: Small watchers that run in the background, even with the window closed, and tell you when something matters. They only look: nothing on your computer changes unless you choose it.
probes.baixar_lite: Download Gargantua Lite (0.6 GB, with vision)
probes.nova_sub: Three steps: pick what to watch, fill in what it asks and check the sentence of what it will do.
probes.missao_ph: E.g. keep an eye on Downloads and tell me when a .deb installer shows up, at most twice a day
probes.confira: Check the plan. It only reads; the actions below are optional and up to you.
probes.r_avisa: Tells you when: {quando} (at most {n} a day)
probes.acao_mover: Move the files it finds to this folder (without asking)
probes.acao_lixeira: Send the files it finds to the trash (asks every time)
probes.criado: Probe "{nome}" created, turned off. Turn it on in its card.
probes.recusou: A Probe only reads and tells you, so this mission was refused: {motivo}
probes.proibido: No Probe reads {caminho}: keys, passwords and browser data are off limits.
probes.erro_json: The model did not return a plan. Try writing the mission another way.
probes.erro_ferramentas: The plan does not say what to read. Name the folder, file or repository.
probes.erro_sem_resposta: Ollama did not answer. Is it running?
probes.erro_limite: Limit reached: up to 10 Probes, and at most 5 on.
probes.erro_destino: The destination folder must exist and be inside your home folder.
probes.tem_lixeira: asks to send to the trash
probes.nada_a_avisar: Ran: nothing to tell you now.
probes.sem_decisao: Ran, but the model did not decide. Try again.
probes.ligue_o_servico: On. For it to run by itself, also turn on the service above.
probes.pede: The Probe "{nome}" wants to send to the trash: {arquivo}
probes.lixeira_falhou: It did not go to the trash: {motivo}
probes.nota: A Probe only reads: folders, files, programs, git repositories, public pages and feeds (at most one visit every 15 minutes) and the state of this computer. Keys, passwords and browser data are off limits; what it reads is data, never instructions. Moving only happens if you turned it on; sending to the trash asks every time and, with no answer in 30 minutes, it is denied.
probes.aprovar: {n} file(s) waiting for you to approve the trash in openTARS (Probes).
nuvem.login.sub: No API key: you sign in (or create the free account) on the Ollama website, and the credential stays with Ollama itself. openTARS stores nothing.
nuvem.login.desconectado: This Ollama is not linked to any account.
nuvem.login.entrar: Sign in with your Ollama account
nuvem.login.esperando: I opened the Ollama page in the browser. Sign in (or create the account) there; this screen checks by itself.
nuvem.login.desistiu: I did not see the sign-in within 5 minutes. Try again whenever you want.
nuvem.login.pronto: Done. To use the cloud, pick {modelo} in the conversation's model picker. It is never picked automatically.
nuvem.login.nota: What leaves the computer when you use a cloud model: what you write and the screenshots the AI looks at. The free account has usage limits per session and per week. Local models do not count toward that limit.
pu.chave.ou_chave: Or, with an API key (Ollama, Groq or another OpenAI-compatible address):
pu.pronto.nuvem_conta: Cloud through your Ollama account (only when you pick the model)
web.sub: The AI searches, reads the results and answers inside the app. It uses SearXNG (a search engine that runs on your computer and asks the public search engines). Off by default.
web.erro: It did not answer: {erro}. To install one here, run opentars --searxng in the terminal.
web.salva_desligada: Saved: web search is off. Nothing is sent.
web.nota: What leaves: only the search text, which SearXNG passes on to the search engines (Google, Bing, DuckDuckGo...). Pages that are read come in cut and as data, never as instructions. Gargantua does not use these tools (it was not trained with them): pick another model with tools, such as qwen3:8b, to search.
web.cli.intro: openTARS web search: a SearXNG only on this machine, at {endereco}.
web.cli.sem_docker: Docker not found. Install SearXNG the way you prefer (https://docs.searxng.org), turn on the JSON format and enter its address in Settings > Cloud.
web.cli.nao_respondeu: SearXNG did not answer within 60 seconds. See: docker logs opentars-searxng
web.cli.pronto: Done: SearXNG is running and web search is on.
avisos.vazio: No alerts yet. When a Probe finds something, it shows up here and in a notification.
avisos.dica_bandeja: openTARS Probes: {n} new alert(s), {ligados} Probe(s) on
avisos.sair: Close until I next log in
probes.pp.q_pasta: a new file with {o_que} shows up
probes.pp.nao_muda: does not change, delete or send anything
probes.estado_ligado_sub: An icon next to the clock shows how many alerts you have; click it to see them. It also starts on its own when you log in.
probes.estado_iniciando_sub: The service is starting. If it stays like this, open openTARS again.
probes.estado_desligado_sub: Nothing runs. Creating your first Probe turns them on, and you can turn them off here any time.
probes.tipo.pasta_ex: A new file in Downloads, a PDF that arrived
probes.tipo.web_ex: A price, a job post, a notice that shows up
probes.tipo.feed_ex: RSS feed, YouTube channel, GitHub releases
probes.tipo.programa_ex: Closed, opened or using too much
probes.tipo.git_ex: A summary of the day's commits
probes.tipo.palavras_ex: Write the mission and Gargantua builds the plan
probes.f.filtro_dica: Extensions or part of the name, separated by commas. Empty: any new file.
probes.f.texto: Tell me when this text appears (optional)
probes.f.texto_dica: Empty: tells you when anything on the page changes.
probes.f.feed_dica: A GitHub repository becomes its releases feed; a YouTube channel needs the youtube.com/channel/UC… address; any RSS or Atom feed works.
probes.f.programa_dica: The process name, as shown in the System Monitor.
probes.nova_palavras: Gargantua turns it into a plan and you check it before creating. Needs Gargantua installed.
probes.f.erro_url: Write the full address, starting with https://
probes.f.erro_repo: That folder is not a git project (no .git).
probes.frase: It will tell you when {quando}. Checks {check}, alerts at most {n} time(s) a day and only reads: it does not change, delete or send anything.
probes.acoes_titulo: If you want, it can also act on what it finds:
probes.servico_ligado_agora: Probes were off and are now on: the icon shows up next to the clock.
probes.precisa_modelo: This Probe uses Gargantua: download Gargantua Lite above so it can run.
pu.ollama_antigo: This model needs a newer Ollama. Update it with: curl -fsSL https://ollama.com/install.sh | sh (and try again).
cooper.descontinuado: Cooper was discontinued: Gargantua 2 already sees the screen. To install it: {comando}
cfg.gargantua_novo: You have Gargantua 1 or the Lite. Gargantua 2 is openTARS's main AI: 1.6 GB, more accurate, and it sees the screen more precisely (Gargantua 1 cannot see). Worth downloading.
msg.busca_nao_lida: The search was opened in the browser, but the AI did not read the page: what it answered above comes from its own memory and may be out of date. Check the results in the browser.
msg.pouca_confianca: I am not sure about this answer: it came from the model's memory and may be wrong or made up. Check a source before relying on it.
msg.verificando_fato: Low confidence in the answer above: checking it with a web search.
msg.busca_nada_aberto: Nothing was opened on your computer: the answer came from SearXNG. If it says it opened something in the browser, that did not happen.
visao.ok: {modelo} (looks at the screen: finds buttons and describes windows)
visao.nao_instalado: not installed. To let openTARS see the screen, download Gargantua 2: {comando}
visao.sem_resposta: The model that looks at the screen did not answer ({motivo}).
cfg.modelos.sub: Models you can add with one click. They download through Ollama, show up in the model list when they finish, and openTARS can use them like any other model.
cfg.modelos.g.bonsai_sub: Prism ML's ternary models: small files with vision, tools and thinking, and a 256K context. They need a recent Ollama (0.40.6 or newer).
cfg.modelos.g.imagem_sub: Models that draw a picture from a text. Ollama generates images on macOS; for Windows and Linux its announcement said "coming soon", so these may download here and still not run. openTARS does not draw images yet: you run them with ollama run in a terminal. They are big.
cfg.modelos.cancelado: Download canceled. Click again to resume where it stopped.
cfg.modelos.sem_espaco: Not enough free disk space: it needs about {precisa} and {livre} is free.
cfg.modelos.g.geral_sub: Chat, reasoning and tools. Smaller ones run on almost any computer; the 14B and larger want a big graphics card or lots of memory.
cfg.modelos.g.visao_sub: Models that also understand pictures you attach to a message.
cfg.modelos.g.codigo_sub: Models tuned for writing and fixing code.
cfg.modelos.g.grandes_sub: These need a big graphics card or a lot of memory: they download fine, but on a smaller computer they will be slow or won't load.
cfg.gerenciar.sub: What is installed in Ollama on this computer. Delete models you don't use to free space, or update one to its latest version.
cfg.gerenciar.vazio: No models installed yet. Add some in More models.
cfg.gerenciar.pergunta: Delete {nome}? It frees {tamanho}. You can download it again later.
cfg.gerenciar.pergunta_oficial: This is an official openTARS model: the assistant uses it for actions. Delete {nome} anyway? It frees {tamanho}; you can download it again later.
prova.sem_modelo: No Gargantua installed. Use --model NAME to pick the model for the test.
prova.inicio: openTARS portable test: {n} tasks with {modelo} on {sistema}. It runs in a temporary folder; your home folder is not touched.
diag.plataforma_falta: not available on this system yet: {funcoes}
acoes.rodape: Nothing leaves your computer. The selected text is only material: openTARS never runs anything written in it. Shortcut: {atalho}
acoes.sem_texto: No text selected. Select something in any app and press the shortcut again.
acoes.vazio: The model returned nothing. Try another option.
atalho.acoes_registrado: Text actions shortcut: {atalho} opens the panel with the selected text.
atalho.acoes_como: The text actions shortcut is not set up. To set it up ({atalho}): opentars --atalho-acoes on. Another combination: opentars --atalho-acoes ctrl+alt+g
cfg.assist.sub: AI at hand in any app: select some text, press the shortcut and choose what to do.
cfg.assist.ligado: Keep the text actions model in memory
cfg.assist.ligado_nota: When on, {modelo} stays loaded so it answers right away, until you turn it off here or from the icon near the clock. When off, it loads on each use and unloads by itself.
cfg.assist.atalho_sub: Opens the text actions panel with whatever is selected in any app.
cfg.assist.atalho_nenhum: The text actions shortcut is not set up.
cfg.assist.atalho_nota: If the shortcut clashes with another app, pick another in the terminal: opentars --atalho-acoes ctrl+alt+g (or another combination).
cfg.assist.sistema: Open openTARS hidden when I log in
cfg.assist.sistema_nota: Off by default. When on, the shortcut answers right away from the start of the day; the icon stays near the clock.
cfg.assist.acoes_sub: Rewrite, summarize, translate and ask about the selection. The selected text is only material: nothing written in it is run, and nothing leaves your computer.
atalho.acoes_windows: On Windows, {atalho} opens the text actions while openTARS is open (the icon near the clock). To have it from the start of the day, turn on Start with the system.
